answers.answer: Select 3 Escape Pods for four players. Place the lowest-numbered in Section A, the next number in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. The bag contains 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults total at four players).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 7 and 10; Key numbers: pod counts and starting bag contents.

answers.answer: Remove Objective cards showing a player count above the actual player count, then shuffle Corporate and Personal decks separately and deal each player one of each, kept hidden. At the First Encounter, each player chooses one of their two and removes the rejected card face down without looking at others' discards. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger that choice; the first Intruder miniature appearing does. The summary does not say the rejected card is removed face down at the deal stage; it says it is removed at First Encounter.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Special Rules, Critical gameplay moments—First Encounter.

answers.answer: Discard the Action card being used and two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2. The two Contamination cards cannot pay any Action cost. If the Action card has sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence: Actions: Action Cost and Actions from Action cards.

answers.answer: The Character takes 1 Light Wound after finishing their own round, including the round in which they take one Action and pass. Once passed, they cannot take more Actions that Player Phase. When passing they may discard any number of cards. Later players' rounds do not make this Character take Fire damage again that turn; Fire damage is assessed at the end of a Character's own round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Player rounds: Fire damage occurs every round only after the Character finishes their own round; passing players take it once at that point.

answers.answer: On entry, flip an unexplored tile face up, reveal and resolve its Exploration token, and return that token to the box. Set the Item count by rotating the tile so the token's number faces the board's Item Counter symbol, except no count is set for the Nest or Room Covered In Slime. Then, if the destination is empty, normally make a Noise roll. Exploration Silence or Danger replaces that roll: Silence means no roll/no effect (unless Slime turns it into Danger); Danger means do not roll, and move all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room, or, if none are eligible, put Noise in every connected Corridor that lacks it. If the destination already contains any Character or Intruder, do not make a Noise roll. The Exploration token is removed from the game into the box after resolution.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll.

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. Instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination. It follows normal movement restrictions, is forbidden in Combat, and cannot be used if every Corridor connected to the destination already has Noise. A Closed Door blocks crossing. Characters cannot stop in Corridors.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions—Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors.

answers.answer: If the rolled Corridor already has Noise, resolve an Encounter. Discard all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance; then draw an Intruder token and place its matching miniature in the Room. Set the drawn token aside outside the bag (it can return if that Intruder type later hides in Technical Corridors). A Blank instead places Noise in every connected Corridor and returns to the bag. Compare the token's number with the triggering player's hand size: Action and Contamination cards both count; fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that player. Contamination therefore counts in the comparison, though it cannot pay Action costs.
answers.evidence: Noise roll; Technical Corridors; Special Rules—Encounters and Blank token in an Encounter.

answers.answer: Danger moves all neighboring Intruders that are not in Combat with any Character into the Room. If none are eligible (including when all are in Combat), place Noise markers in every connected Corridor that lacks one. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter. A Character with Slime resolves Danger instead of Silence.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens—Danger and Silence; Noise roll; Encounters.

answers.answer: In an Encounter, a Blank places a Noise marker in each connected Corridor. If it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if one is available; then return the Blank to the bag. In bag development, drawing a Blank adds an Adult token if available regardless of whether the Blank was the last token, then returns the Blank to the bag.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Blank token in an Encounter; Turn Structure—Intruder bag development, Blank.

answers.answer: Neither Intruder moves through the Closed Door; the Door is destroyed, and both stay in their starting Room. A destroyed Door lies flat and cannot be closed again (except with the Plasma Torch Item). An Intruder appearing due to a Noise roll is not blocked by a Closed Door.
answers.evidence: Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers—Door tokens.

answers.answer: The Intruder disappears from the board into the ducts: remove its miniature, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the Intruder bag. The Noise marker already on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors (exceptions are the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item); Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors.

answers.answer: Both Shoot and Melee cost 1 Action card and target one Intruder in the Character's Room. Shoot requires a Weapon in Hand with Ammo and discards 1 Ammo; it does not add a Contamination card. Melee draws a Contamination card onto the Action discard pile. A Melee miss inflicts a Serious Wound; a Shoot miss has no Melee miss penalty. A double-hit result deals 2 Injuries when Shooting but only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: Combat—Shoot and Melee Attack; Combat quick reference.

answers.answer: After placing Injury markers, a Larva dies at 1 Injury and is removed; no Carcass is placed for Larvae. An Adult is checked by drawing one Intruder Attack card: if its blood value is equal to or lower than its injury count, it dies and a Carcass is placed in the Room. A Queen is checked by drawing two cards, adding their blood values, and comparing the sum to its injuries; on death, a Carcass is placed. If a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow on either card, the Queen flees via a Corridor selected by an Event card. The summary does not specify a separate priority rule between a death result and retreat arrow on the same check.
answers.evidence: Combat—Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack for each of the two Intruders, with the escaper as the target. If the Character dies, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, they move to the neighboring Room, exploring it if unexplored and making a Noise roll if the destination is empty.
answers.evidence: Combat—Character Escape; Intruder Attack.

answers.answer: The Intruder targets the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the Character with the First Player token, or the next player in turn order. A hit occurs when the drawn Intruder Attack card shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder; otherwise it misses. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove its miniature from the board, put it on the target's Character board, and give the target one Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Combat—Intruder Attack and Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards.

answers.answer: Dressing a Serious Wound suppresses its effect but it still counts toward the three-wound limit, so at three Serious Wounds any additional Wound kills the Character, even if one wound is dressed. Otherwise, a third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies. On death, remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room as an Object, and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Wounds and Death; Heavy Objects.

answers.answer: Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the Character's hand, removing non-Infected cards. An Infected result places a Larva on the Character board; if a Larva is already there, the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the deck, hand, and discard pile, removes all Infected ones, and removes a Larva if present. It then causes 1 Light Wound and an automatic pass; shuffle all cards, including the whole hand and remaining Contamination, into the Action deck. The hand stays empty until the next turn.
answers.evidence: Room Actions—Surgery, Canteen, Shower Room; Contamination cards and Infection.

answers.answer: Shoot or Melee against uncarried Eggs: each Injury destroys one Egg. Melee against Eggs never draws Contamination and a miss causes no Wound. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov Cocktail destroys 1. Each separate attempt to destroy an Egg is followed by a Noise roll. A Fire marker destroys 1 uncarried Egg during each Fire Damage step. When no Eggs remain, the Nest is destroyed and is marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest; Combat quick reference.

answers.answer: Use the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action, paying 2 Action cards; the Pod must be Unlocked and have a free Character space in that Section. Resolve a Noise roll first. Entry fails if an Intruder appears or is present in the Room, and entry is also barred if the Room has a Malfunction marker. Each Pod holds up to 2 Characters; Heavy Objects take no Character space. After entering, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, launch at the start of your first round in each Player Phase or exit voluntarily for free; if you do not launch during your round, you automatically pass. If an Intruder appears in the Evacuation Section Room while you wait, all Characters in its Pods return to that Room.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods; Room Actions—Evacuation Section A/B.

answers.answer: The Victory Check order is Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. If two Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders; launched Pods are already away. If the ship is headed somewhere other than Earth, hibernating Characters die, except a Character with the Quarantine Objective survives hibernation if the destination is Mars. That Objective requires Mars, and the summary also states a ship-reach-Earth/Mars objective requires the right Coordinates and at least 2 Working Engines. For Contamination, each surviving Character, evacuated or hibernating, is checked: scan all cards; if any is Infected, shuffle all cards and draw four, and any Contamination card among those four kills. A Larva triggers that draw-four test directly, skipping the initial scan. Thus Pod passengers do need the Contamination check.
answers.evidence: Victory Check; Objective types; Overview.
